transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm a graphic designer, and after getting promoted to a senior role with a lot of high-profile projects last year, I've really been struggling with my eating. When I’m alone working late, I start eating and it feels like I can’t stop or control how much I’m eating until it’s over. A colleague recently suggested I might be using food to cope with the stress, which made me realize I need to seek help.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever do things to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do anything like that to try to prevent weight gain. I've never made myself throw up, used laxatives, or tried to fast or over-exercise after an episode. I just have to live with how uncomfortable and heavy I feel.
How often do these episodes of losing control over your eating occur, and how many months has this been going on?

These episodes have been happening at least once a week for about ten months now, and sometimes even more often when my work deadlines pile up. It started shortly after I took on the senior designer role and all the big projects hit at once.
During these episodes, do you typically eat much faster than normal, eat until you feel uncomfortably full, or eat large amounts even when you aren't feeling hungry?

Yes, all of those are true—I eat incredibly fast, barely chewing or tasting the food, often starting even when I'm not hungry at all and just finished a normal dinner. I don't stop until my stomach is so physically tight and bloated that it actually hurts to sit up straight.
How do you feel emotionally after these episodes? Do you often experience intense feelings of guilt, disgust with yourself, or sadness afterward?

Yes, I feel deeply ashamed and embarrassed about how much I've eaten, to the point where I just want to hide in my apartment and avoid seeing anyone. The next day, I feel incredibly sluggish and mentally foggy, which makes me feel completely out of step with the organized, curated life I usually pride myself on.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with recurrent episodes of binge eating characterized by eating large amounts of food rapidly, eating until uncomfortably full, eating when not physically hungry, and experiencing intense guilt, shame, and distress afterward. These episodes have occurred at least once a week for 10 months, triggered by work-related stress. The absence of recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors (such as purging, laxative misuse, fasting, or excessive exercise) rules out Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2), confirming a diagnosis of Binge Eating Disorder, classified under Other Eating Disorders (F50.8 in ICD-10).
